arxiv-2510-25579.title: Population of Binary Black Holes Inferred from One Hundred and Fifty Gravitational Wave Signals. 2026 Population of Binary Black Holes Inferred from One Hundred and Fifty Gravitational Wave Signals. – B
arxiv-2510-25579.creator: Vaibhav Tiwari
arxiv-2510-25579.description: Abstract The LIGO–Virgo–KAGRA collaborations have reported GW ( GW ) signals from more than 150 BBH in the fourth catalog (GWTC-4). Here, we investigate the population properties of these BBH using the mixture-model framework Vamana. We present one-dimensional distributions of masses and spins, explore their correlations, and examine their evolution with redshift.

Matrix metalloproteinase-19 (MMP19) affects cell proliferation, adhesion, and migration in vitro but its physiological role in vivo is poorly understood. The observation that suicides sometimes cluster in space and/or time has led to suggestions that these clusters are caused by the social learning of suicide-related behaviours, or “copycat suicides”. pmc-11444735.title: Effects of selective stimulation of apical electrodes on temporal pitch perception by cochlear implant recipients
pmc-11444735.creator: Evelien De Groote, Robert P. Carlyon, John M. Deeks, Olivier Macherey
pmc-11444735.description: This study investigated whether selective apical stimulation improves temporal pitch perception in eight MED-EL cochlear implant recipients and whether any such improvement relates to auditory-nerve survival. Three stimulation conditions differing in the place and width of excitation were evaluated: single-electrode stimulation of (i) the most apical, (ii) a mid-array electrode, and (iii) multi-electrode stimulation of the four most apical electrodes.

pmc-11481596.title: Immune protective, stress indicators, antioxidant, histopathological status, and heat shock protein gene expression impacts of dietary Bacillus spp. against heat shock in Nile tilapia, Oreochromis niloticus
pmc-11481596.creator: Samia Elbahnaswy, Gehad E Elshopakey, Abdelwahab A Abdelwarith, Elsayed M Younis, Simon J Davies, Mai A M El-Son
pmc-11481596.description: This research evaluated the efficacy of mixed Bacillus strains probiotic supplements in mitigating acute thermal-induced stress in Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus). Three experimental fish groups involved 135 Nile tilapia (49 ± 2 g); one control (no added probiotics), 0.5, and 1% of selected Bacillus strains (B. subtilis, B. licheniformis, and B. pumilus) for 58 days.

pmc-11630257.title: Identification and characterization of human KALRN mRNA and Kalirin protein isoforms
pmc-11630257.creator: Arne W Mould, David J Wright, Klaus D Bornemann, Bastian Hengerer, Rob Pinnock, Edward Drydale, James Bancroft, Nicola A L Hall, Annette von Delft, Paul E Brennan, Paul J Harrison, Wilfried Haerty, Elizabeth M Tunbridge
pmc-11630257.description: Kalirin is a multidomain protein with important roles in neurite outgrowth, and synaptic spine formation and remodeling. Genetic and pathophysiological links with various neuropsychiatric disorders associated with synaptic dysfunction and cognitive impairment have sparked interest in its potential as a pharmacological target.

pmc-12569446.title: Co‐creating an everyday language illustration of learning health systems alongside patient, caregiver, and community partners
pmc-12569446.creator: Shelley Vanderhout, Maureen Smith, Nakia Lee‐Foon, Amanda Doherty‐Kirby, Rona Fleming, Don Grant, Annie‐Danielle Grenier, John Grogan, Roger Farley, Margaret King, Chris Johnston, Virgil Luca, Lisa Ridgway, Donna Rubenstein, Candace Skrapek, Kerry Kuluski
pmc-12569446.description: IntroductionPatients, caregivers, and community partners (PCC) can have a variety of roles in learning health systems (LHS), such as contributing their data from healthcare encounters to embedded, continuous engagement where they identify health system priorities, guide operational, research, and quality improvement decisions, and facilitate knowledge sharing and implementation.

pmc-12716837.title: Applying 3D correlative structured illumination microscopy and X-ray tomography to characterise herpes simplex virus-1 morphogenesis
pmc-12716837.creator: Kamal L Nahas, Viv Connor, Kaveesha J Wijesinghe, Henry G Barrow, Ian M Dobbie, Maria Harkiolaki, Stephen C Graham, Colin M Crump, Laura Ruth Delgui, Kamal L Nahas, Viv Connor, Kaveesha J Wijesinghe, Henry G Barrow, Ian M Dobbie, Maria Harkiolaki, Stephen C Graham, Colin M Crump
pmc-12716837.description: Numerous viral genes are involved in the assembly of herpes simplex virus-1 (HSV-1), but their relative importance and function remain poorly characterised. Transmission electron microscopy has been used to study viral protein function in cells infected with HSV-1 mutants; however, these studies were usually conducted without correlative light microscopy to identify specific viral components.

pmc-13054970.title: Ethical design as a prerequisite for translational microbiome science
pmc-13054970.creator: Jo-Ann S Passmore, Abigail Nieves Delgado, Anna-Ursula Happel
pmc-13054970.description: Human microbiome research is expanding globally, yet remains dominated by samples, institutions, and leadership from the Global North. This imbalance undermines scientific validity, as microbiomes are shaped by socio-ecological context and temporal dynamics, and risks producing diagnostics and therapeutics that are not applicable across diverse populations. In this comment, we engage with van Daele et al.

pmc-13222876.title: Spatiotemporal dynamics of carbon emissions induced by land-use change and their implications for climate resilience in West African drylands
pmc-13222876.creator: Issaka Abdou Razakou Kiribou, Kangbéni Dimobe, Tiga Neya, Sintayehu W Dejene
pmc-13222876.description: Understanding the effects of land-use and land-cover change (LULC) on carbon emissions is crucial for ensuring the sustainable management of dryland ecosystems. This study investigates spatial and temporal changes in carbon stock associated with LULC in one of the key biodiversity hotspots of the West African drylands.

pmc-13299052.title: Association Between Electronic Device Usage, Physical Activity, and Sleep Quality Related to Cervicogenic Headache Among College Students in Saudi Arabia
pmc-13299052.creator: Shahul Hameed Pakkir Mohamed, Abdulaziz A. Albalwi, Mohamed Taher Mahmoud Eldesoky, Hamad S. Al Amer, Ahmad A. Alharbi, Jana Alhmeed, Emtenan Alhakami, Shahad Battal Alanazi, Maha Alrashedi, Ghala Dakhilallah
pmc-13299052.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background and Objectives: Cervicogenic headaches (CGH) are increasingly common among college students and may negatively affect academic performance and sleep quality. This study aimed to identify the self-reported prevalence of cervicogenic-type head and neck pain in a convenience sample of Saudi college students and to examine its associations with electronic device use, physical activity, and sleep quality among college students in Saudi Arabia.

pmc-13309410.title: Assessing Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms in Women Practising Competitive Judo: Findings from a Cross-sectional Study
pmc-13309410.creator: Aleksandra Saulicz, Mariola Saulicz, Edward Saulicz
pmc-13309410.description: Introduction and HypothesisHigh impact physical activity (PA) in sportswomen is a risk factor for the development of stress-induced urinary incontinence and potentially for other dysfunctions of the pelvic floor. This study was aimed at assessing the occurrence of lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS) in professional female judo practitioners.
